questions.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.why: Zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for general truths.

questions.q: If water reaches 100°C, it ___.
questions.why: Zero conditional describes scientific facts with present simple.

questions.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ the picnic.
questions.why: First conditional uses 'will' in the result clause for likely future situations.

questions.q: If she ___ hard, she will pass the exam.
questions.why: After 'if' in the first conditional, use present simple, not 'will'.

questions.q: I ___ you as soon as I arrive.
questions.why: First conditional: the main clause takes 'will' for a future result.

questions.q: If I ___ rich, I would buy a yacht.
questions.why: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons in the 'if' clause.

questions.q: If he ___ more time, he would learn the guitar.
questions.why: Second conditional uses past simple in the 'if' clause for unreal present situations.

questions.q: If I were you, I ___ that offer.
questions.why: Second conditional uses 'would' in the result clause for hypothetical advice.

questions.q: What ___ you do if you won the lottery?
questions.why: Second conditional questions about unreal situations use 'would'.

questions.q: If they had left earlier, they ___ the train.
questions.why: Third conditional uses 'would have + past participle' for unreal past results.

questions.q: If she ___ harder, she would have passed.
questions.why: Third conditional uses past perfect in the 'if' clause for the unreal past.

questions.q: I would have helped you if you ___ me.
questions.why: Third conditional pairs past perfect ('had asked') with 'would have'.

questions.q: If I had taken that job, I ___ in London now.
questions.why: Mixed conditional: past condition with a present result uses 'would + base verb'.

questions.q: If she weren't so shy, she ___ that speech yesterday.
questions.why: Mixed conditional: present condition with a past result uses 'would have + past participle'.

questions.q: If I had saved more money, I ___ a car today.
questions.why: Mixed conditional links a past cause to a present result with 'would + base verb'.

questions.q: ___ you study, you will fail the test.
questions.why: 'Unless' means 'if not' and introduces the only condition that avoids the result.

questions.q: We won't go out ___ the rain stops.
questions.why: 'Unless the rain stops' means 'if the rain does not stop'.

questions.q: I wish I ___ taller.
questions.why: 'Wish' about the present uses past simple, with 'were' for all persons.

questions.q: I wish I ___ how to swim.
questions.why: 'Wish' + past simple expresses a regret about a present situation.

questions.q: If only I ___ harder for that exam last year.
questions.why: 'If only' + past perfect expresses regret about the past.

questions.q: I wish I ___ that rude email yesterday.
questions.why: 'Wish' about a past regret uses the past perfect.

questions.q: If only she ___ here to see this!
questions.why: 'If only' about an unreal present uses past simple, with 'were' for all persons.

questions.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.why: 'Unless' clauses follow first-conditional patterns, so the result uses 'will'.

questions.q: If I ___ you were ill, I would have visited.
questions.why: Third conditional uses past perfect after 'if' for an unreal past condition.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'If you mix blue and yellow, you ___ green.' (get)
questions.why: Zero conditional uses present simple for a general truth.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'If it ___ tomorrow, I'll take an umbrella.' (rain)
questions.why: After 'if' in the first conditional, use present simple.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'If I ___ you, I'd apologise.' (be)
questions.why: Second conditional prefers 'were' for all persons, though 'was' is common in speech.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'If they had asked, I ___ helped them.' (would)
questions.why: Third conditional uses 'would have + past participle' for the result.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I wish I ___ more languages.' (speak)
questions.why: 'Wish' about the present uses past simple.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'We'll stay home ___ the weather improves.' (if not, one word)
questions.why: 'Unless' means 'if not' and introduces the saving condition.
